title: Composition isomorphism of pushforwards of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$, $g\colon Y\to Z$
morphisms of schemes. There is a natural isomorphism

$$
g_*\circ f_*\cong(g\circ f)_*\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Z}
$$

of pushforwards of module objects ([def-sfb-module-lower-star]) whose underlying
isomorphism of sheaves is the composition isomorphism
$g^{\Ab}_*f^{\Ab}_*M\cong(g\circ f)^{\Ab}_*M$ of pushforwards of abelian sheaves.

proof.text: Write $P=f_*^{\Ab}$, $Q=g_*^{\Ab}$, $H=(g\circ f)_*^{\Ab}$ and $R_T=\Lambda_T$ for $T=X,Y,Z$. For a module $M$ write $\gamma_M:R_X\otimes M\to M$ for its action. The underlying sheaves of $g_*f_*M$ and $(g\circ f)_*M$ are $QPM$ and $HM$ by [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Let $c:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ be the monoidal natural isomorphism of [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal], applied with $\mathcal A=\Ab$ (explicitly included among its instances). Denote the lax monoidal tensor maps by $m^P,m^Q,m^H$ and put $m^{QP}_{A,B}=Q(m^P_{A,B})\circ m^Q_{PA,PB}$. We construct the required component using the sheaf map $c_M$.

source.place: Composition-isomorphisms bullet; underlying functor in the pushforward bullet

proof.text:
Expand the action on $g_*f_*M$ using the action formula of [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Set $\delta=Q(\eta_f)\circ\eta_g:R_Z\to QPR_X$. Its action $a_M:R_Z\otimes QPM\to QPM$ is
$$a_M=Q\bigl(P(\gamma_M)\circ m^P_{R_X,M}\circ(\eta_f\otimes1_{PM})\bigr)\circ m^Q_{R_Y,PM}\circ(\eta_g\otimes1_{QPM})
=QP(\gamma_M)\circ m^{QP}_{R_X,M}\circ(\delta\otimes1_{QPM}).$$
The equality is functoriality of $Q$ and the naturality identity
$$Q(\eta_f\otimes1_{PM})\circ m^Q_{R_Y,PM}=m^Q_{PR_X,PM}\circ(Q(\eta_f)\otimes1_{QPM}).$$
This also explains directly, on actions, the transport/restriction interchange implicit in the imported proof; no separate interchange theorem is assumed. The transport action is exactly that of [sk-def-sfb-transport], clause 1.

Let $b_M=H(\gamma_M)\circ m^H_{R_X,M}\circ(\eta_{g\circ f}\otimes1_{HM})$ be the action on $(g\circ f)_*M$ from [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Naturality of $c$ at $\gamma_M$ and its monoidality ([lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal]) give
$$\begin{aligned}
c_M\circ a_M
&=H(\gamma_M)\circ c_{R_X\otimes M}\circ m^{QP}_{R_X,M}\circ(\delta\otimes1)\\
&=H(\gamma_M)\circ m^H_{R_X,M}\circ(c_{R_X}\otimes c_M)\circ(\delta\otimes1)\\
&=H(\gamma_M)\circ m^H_{R_X,M}\circ((c_{R_X}\circ\delta)\otimes c_M)\\
&=b_M\circ(1_{R_Z}\otimes c_M).
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality uses precisely $c_{R_X}\circ\delta=\eta_{g\circ f}$ from [lem-sfb-eta-comp], with its pushforwards interpreted as abelian-sheaf pushforwards. Thus $c_M$ is an $R_Z$-module morphism by the definition in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], clause 2.

source.place: Displayed composition identity, combined with the tensor compatibility in lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal

proof.text:
The inverse sheaf map is linear as well: the equality in step 3, precomposed with $1_{R_Z}\otimes c_M^{-1}$ and postcomposed with $c_M^{-1}$, gives
$$c_M^{-1}\circ b_M=a_M\circ(1_{R_Z}\otimes c_M^{-1}).$$
The two composites are identities because their underlying sheaf maps are identities; module morphisms consist of their underlying maps with a linearity condition ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects], clause 2). For a module morphism $u:M\to N$, both pushforwards act on its underlying map by $QP(u)$ and $H(u)$, since transport commutes with forgetful functors ([sk-def-sfb-transport], clause 1), and restriction of scalars is the identity on underlying objects and morphisms ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], clause 1), as used in [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Naturality of the sheaf isomorphism $c$ says $H(u)\circ c_M=c_N\circ QP(u)$; this is the required naturality in the module category. The linear maps $c_M$ and $c_M^{-1}$ therefore define the natural isomorphism, with exactly the required underlying sheaf isomorphism.
